scope: Source feasibility/self-review, not independent acceptance; no diagnostic implementation or execution.
source_findings: Existing common graph has distinct restore, suffix/resolve, tile composition and complete target-copy owners; controls preserve those owners and introduce no replacement shader.

Installed wgpu encoder timestamps require TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_ENCODERS and explicitly warn about reordering. Vulkan adapter enables encoder/pass timestamp features together when timestamp_valid_bits>=36; actual enabled capability is checked once on diagnostic launch.

Installed Vulkan encoder uses BOTTOM_OF_PIPE timestamp writes. This supports whole-graph diagnostics but not treating timestamps as arbitrary memory barriers or proving zero perturbation. N/D/M completion controls are mandatory.
Frozen preparation control is accepted only with identical uploaded bytes and command manifest. Its implementation feasibility is a pre-GPU gate, not permission to duplicate the renderer.

Common preinitialized T/R make draw-free controls defined and mutually comparable, but initialization/serialized cadence can alter cache/scheduling. No literal historical percentile decomposition or universal hardware floor.

external_reference.use: Search result corroborates execution dependency description; full page retrieval was unavailable. Installed source and conservative public-wgpu warning control the proposed method; no stronger guarantee inferred.

review_outcome: Concrete bounded proposed experiment. Correctness, exact operation parity and timestamp support remain explicit post-approval prerequisites. Failure or inconclusive outcome ends the study; no redesign, alternate clock or extended sampling.
